title: Graceful throttle and tenant sandbox concept
content:
Purpose

This doc sketches a lightweight, operationally pragmatic approach for handling transient demand surges on Dedicated capacity without forcing immediate capacity purchases or blunt evictions. Goal: keep tenant workloads alive with predictable degradation, preserve SLOs for paying tiers, and give operators clear knobs to control risk.

Problem we see in the wild

- Sudden tenant spikes (cron jobs, model retrains, malformed loops, bursty user traffic) cause noisy neighbors or full node saturation.
- Customers want low-latency guarantees but don’t want to overcommit to reserved capacity for every tail spike.
- Current fallbacks are binary: block/evict or let everything contend. Both are bad: evictions are customer-facing downtime; full contention harms high-value customers.

High-level idea

Introduce two complementary features: a) Tenant Sandbox lanes (soft isolation pool for transient oversubscription) and b) Graceful Throttle lanes (degraded-quality, credit-driven throttle that prioritizes SLO-preserving requests). Together they allow short-lived oversubscription without permanent capacity changes or noisy evictions.

Key concepts

- Sandbox Pool: a small, automatically provisioned buffer of capacity (GPU/slots) reserved for short-lived spikes. Tenants with sudden demand are diverted to sandbox lane where they get best-effort throughput and limited time window (e.g., 5–30 minutes). Sandbox is isolated at the scheduling level (scheduling priority, KV cache namespace limits, network qdisc shapers).

- Graceful Throttle: instead of hard rejects or dropping requests, throttle non-critical routes by applying controlled latency (token-based pacing), reduced KV cache allocation, and optional model-slimming (lower-precision quantized variant) within configured risk bands. Throttled requests are labeled and traced for billing/monitoring.

- Credit Ledger: a per-tenant short-lived credit balance accrued from burst allowances (paid tiers get higher base credits). Credits are consumed when using Sandbox or Graceful Throttle. Ledger supports expiration (e.g., credits reset after 24h) and emergency top-ups by ops.

- Safety Escalation: automated fallback to more aggressive measures (queued requests, longer throttles, preemptive soft-eviction) only if sandbox + throttle thresholds exceeded or if SRE health signals degrade.

Why this is different from existing approaches

- Not just autoscale up: autoscaling is still the end-state for persistent demand, but autoscale has latency and cost. Sandbox + graceful throttle bridge the immediate gap with predictable semantics.
- Not just LIFO eviction: we avoid noisy evictions by offering a degradable execution lane.

API & Controls (customer-facing)

Config knobs (per-tenant or per-reservation):
- burst_window_seconds: 300–1800 (default 600s)
- sandbox_enabled: true/false
- sandbox_max_rate: requests/sec or tokens/sec that can be admitted to sandbox
- throttle_profile: [pacing_ms, cache_fraction, model_variant] e.g., [50ms, 0.5, small-quant]
- credit_allocation: base credits per day (numbers by tier)
- emergency_policy: auto-fallback | ops-review | reject

Metrics & Observability (console + telemetry)

- sandbox_admissions_count (per-tenant)
- sandbox_rejection_count
- credits_balance (gauge)
- throttle_applied_rate (percentage of requests)
- pct_of_tokens_generated_in_sandbox
- latency_by_lane and quality_delta_by_lane (BLEU/ROUGE proxy or custom eval hooks)
- correlated signals: node_gpu_util, node_mem_pressure, kv_cache_evictions

- Console: per-route view that shows how often a tenant used sandbox/throttle and estimated cost delta. Alerting templates: sandbox_usage_high, credit_depleted, graceful_throttle_regression

Operational semantics (ops perspective)

Admission flow (simplified):
1) Incoming request arrives. Scheduler checks tenant state and current node headroom.
2) If node overloaded and tenant has credits + sandbox_enabled, request can be routed into Sandbox or Throttle depending on routing policy.
3) Sandbox queue uses best-effort scheduling: reduced parallelism, controlled preemption, separate KV namespace. Throttle lane introduces pacing and lower cache fraction.
4) Credits are decremented atomically; admission logged for billing.
5) If credits hit zero and node still saturated, escalate to emergency policy (possibly reject or send to lower-tier model).

Isolation surfaces and implementation notes

- Scheduling: mark sandbox pods with lower QoS class (but not eviction-prone); prefer bin-packing that isolates sandbox onto nodes with spare NVMe or CPU headroom.
- KV cache: sandbox tenants get namespaced caches and lower cache residency budgets to avoid polluting hot KV slots.
- CUDA/GPU: use CUDA streams with constrained concurrency and smaller KV cache slices. For quantized variants, use lower memory footprint kernels.
- Networking: token bucket qdisc per-tenant in sandbox to flatten bursts to steady throughput.
- Tracing: add \"lane=sandbox|throttle\" tag to requests so downstream logs/metrics break out lanes easily.

Billing and commercial considerations

- Default behavior: sandbox consumption is billed at a premium delta (e.g., 2x host reservation rate) to reflect headroom cost. Credits can offset billing.
- Enterprise customers can opt into higher burst allowances or turn sandbox off entirely.
- Need clear docs and pricing examples. Example: 10 credits = one average long-generation in sandbox; show cost delta.

Interaction with autoscaling

- Autoscaler should be conservative while sandbox is actively used: sandbox is short-term stopgap, not substitute for persistent autoscale.
- Heuristic: if sandbox use > X% of time over Y window (e.g., 30% for 24h), trigger autoscale recommendation and a flag in console.

Launch plan and experiments

Phase 0 - Engineering spike (2 weeks): implement admission tagging, credit ledger prototype, and simulated throttle profile in staging.
Phase 1 - Canary (4 weeks): enable for internal customers and few low-risk tenants, monitor quality regressions.
Phase 2 - Opt-in beta (8 weeks): allow customers to opt-in; collect billing and UX feedback.
Phase 3 - Gradual roll (quarterly): enroll default behavior with conservative defaults; provide migration docs.

Success metrics

- Reduction in customer-facing evictions by 80% during transient spikes.
- Maintain p95 latency for gold tier within x% of baseline while sandbox is used for lower tiers.
- Fewer emergency support incidents related to noisy neighbors.
- Autoscale conversion: fraction of tenants that move to permanent capacity after repeated sandbox use (should be > 60% flagged for sales ops outreach).

Open questions / TODOs

- Credit economics: how many credits to allocate by tier? Pricing model for paid credits vs included allowance. (Action: finance + pricing)
- Model-slimming safety: what models are safe to use as lower-quality fallbacks (LLM families, tokenization parity). (Action: applied-ml)
- Precise sandbox sizing: global % of cluster vs per-region pools. (Action: infra + capacity)
- SLA language: how do we describe sandbox in contracts without exposing risk? Draft suggested SLA clause. (Action: legal)
- UX: Console UI for fast viewing (one-click disable sandbox for tenant). (Action: product-dex)

Notes to self

- Keep sandbox admission as transparent as possible to customers: label events but avoid surprising behavior.
- We should fail closed on billing instrumentation: always log consumption.
- Prioritize small-scope experiments (start with throttle-only) to get telemetry before introducing cache isolation.

Appendix: quick checklist for engineering spike

- [ ] Add admission tag to request path and storage for lane history
- [ ] Implement in-memory credit ledger with TTL semantics
- [ ] Create throttle middleware that can apply pacing and cache fraction header
- [ ] Prototype namespace isolation for KV cache and evictions
- [ ] Dashboard widgets for sandbox usage and credit balance
- [ ] Small-scale canary on non-production cluster

References / related tickets

- ENG-2345: prototype credit ledger
- RUNTIME-678: scheduler admission hooks
- CONSOLE-122: sandbox analytics view

End of sketch.

If this approach sounds reasonable, next step: pick 2 tenants for a 2-week throttle-only canary and surface initial telemetry.
